item.title: WATCH | Boer goats evolved beyond their use for manure
item.description: In the Clanwilliam area, meat production was not always the primary focus of Boer goat farming; sixty years ago, their manure played a much more significant role in vegetable and roll tobacco cultivation.

item.title: Land Bank services continue despite cyberattack
item.description: Following a cyberattack in January, Land Bank’s website is still down, but the bank assures clients that it is open for business via its relationship managers.

item.title: FMD | ‘It’s an emergency situation’ – Steenhuisen on vaccination liability clauses
item.description: There are livestock farmers who are baulking at the national Department of Agriculture’s requirements to be indemnified against any potential negative consequences of vaccinating South Africa’s cattle and other species against foot-and-mouth disease (FMD). John Steenhuisen, the Minister of Agriculture, says this indemnification is not driven by ulterior motives.

item.title: El Niño: Strong indications of below-average rainfall
item.description: Current meteorological models indicate a high probability of below-normal precipitation during the anticipated El Niño event, spanning November 2026 through April 2027, with peak impacts expected during the December-March period.

item.title: FMD | Royal Agricultural Show postponed until October
item.description: South Africa’s current foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) epidemic has claimed yet another victim. The Royal Agricultural Show, which was initially scheduled to be held from 29 May to 3 June at its new home at Tweedie Hall in KwaZulu-Natal, has been postponed until sometime in October.

item.title: SA fruit industry tastes sweet success in India and China
item.description: The South African fruit industry has started the year on a positive note. Four times more apples were exported to India this year compared to 2023, while plums were exported to China for the first time.

item.title: Switzerland-based global platform calls SA conference to address FMD crisis
item.description: The International Forum for Transboundary Animal Diseases and Food Safety (TAFS Forum), a Switzerland-based global platform that brings together stakeholders to address cross-border animal health threats, will host a crucial regional conference in Cape Town this month to tackle the growing challenge of foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) in Southern Africa.

item.title: Attack on Iran already hits oil prices
item.description: Although the long-term consequences of the US and Israeli attacks on Iran are still unclear, there is no doubt it will push fuel prices higher in the short term.
